newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Telephone: 11-3324842, 11-3761233; Fax: 91-11-3351006 Internet : biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com
TOP STORIES
Hindustan Times
TUSSLE FOR MORE UP SEATS HOTS UP IN UNITED FRONT

A tussle for more seats is intensifying in the United Front (UF) government for assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh (UP). The latest entrant in the coalition, Bharatiya Kisan Kamgar Party (BKKP) chief Ajit Singh, is reported to have demanded 40 out of total of 425 seats at stake in the polls. Ajit Singh recently left the Congress party to join hands with the UF. Ajit Singh, along with other BKKP leader M S Tikait, commands considerable support in western parts of UP. A major UF constituent, the Samajwadi Party, is also said be talking with other UF partners, including Left parties, on seat sharing.
Indian Express
GOVERNMENT FAILURE ON EX-CHIEF MINISTER UPSETS ALLIES

The DMK and Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party leaders are upset with the United Front (UF) government for failure to ask the Central Investigative Agency to investigate alleged cases of corruption against former Tamil Nadu chief minister Jayalaitha. The DMK and TMC are both members of the UF. Both parties made the allegations a camaign issue in general elections in May
Times Of India
OUTGOING NAVAL CHIEF BLAMES GOVERNMENT ON ALLOCATIONS

The outgoing Chief of Naval Staff, Admiral Vijay Singh Shekawat, said low budget allocations had caused a decline in navy levels and had an impact on its operational readiness. Painting a grim future for the navy, he said the force was plagued by bureaucratic delays and a lack of understanding of navy matters by the government. India had not placed one order for a major warship in the last 10 years. Most of the existing vessels were likely to be decommissioned from the year 2000.
Economic Times
TELECOM DEPARTMENT CUTS INTERCONNECT RATES BY 30 PCT

The Department of Telecommunication (DoT) cut interconnect charges by 30 percent and waived registration fees for basic services operators. It also reduced the interconnect charges for a two megabit link from 136,000 rupees per annum to 96,000 rupees per annum. In addition, it removed the one-time 90,000 rupee registration fee to be paid by each basic operator for connecting a two megabit link with DoT's exchanges.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS TO PUT ERRING FIRMS ON NOTICE

The finance ministry is working on a comprehensive strategy to check the high incidence of financial irregularities in corporate houses at the cost of banks, Financial Institutions (FIs) and shareholders. The ministry has asked FIs to act in order to check defaults, fraud and any other acts that go against the interests of shareholders in the case of corporates, where they have either an equity or loan exposure, or both.
DLF POWER MAPS PLAN TO PRODUCE 1,500 MW BY 2000

DLF Power has drawn up plans to set up an estimated 1,500 MW of generating capacity in greenfield power projects by the year 2000. It has decided to carry on with its power projects without any strategic tie ups. DLF has won projects totalling an estimated 500 MW in Rajasthan, Haryana, West Bengal, Assam, Bihar and Karnataka. It has also bid for a 330 MW project in Uttar Pradesh. DLF sources said the power purchase agreements for projects in Rajasthan, Haryana and Karnataka were in various stages of finalisation. Work on eight smaller projects totalling an estimated 90 MW in Assam, Bihar and West Bengal had already started, the sources added.
Financial Express
MULTINATIONALS MAY UPSTAGE NTPC, RPG PLANS FOR GAS STATIONS

Oil majors Amoco and Uncool, have joined the race to promote the two 1,000-MW power projects which will be based on feedstock from giant liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminals coming up soon on the east and west coasts. The terminals, based on imported LNG, are being jointly promoted by the India Oil Corp, the Oil and Natural Gas Corp and the Gas Authority of India Ltd. The entry of Amoco and Uncool may upstage National Thermal Power Corp and RP Goenka group's plans to build these power projects.
Financial Express
HALDIA NAPHTHA PLANT IN A LIMBO

The failure of the State Bank of India to give a guarantee of 1.4 billion rupees to the Japan's Exim Bank for Haldia Petrochem has held up the naphtha cracker plant, the core of the project. The 51.7 billion rupee project is one of the largest beneficiaries of foreign direct investment in the country. The Toyo Engineering Corporation, the contractor for plant, has refused to start work unless it received guarantees from the financial institutions.
INFLATION RISES TO 5.71 PCT

The annual rate of inflation continued its upwards trend for the third successive week. It gained 0.17 percentage points to touch 5.71 percent for the week ended August 24. The recent hike in petroleum prices led to a spurt in inflation as it rose up by 0.67 percentage points during the last three weeks. Except for a brief lull during the week ending August 3, it had earlier gained 1.1 percentage points during the four previous weeks ending July 27. It was placed at 8.6 percent during the corresponding period of the previous year.
GOVERNMENT WEIGHS CAP ON PUBLIC DEBT

The government plans to impose a statutory ceiling on the level of public debt as part of a strategy to improve fiscal management. The strategy requires that once the debt stocks have been identified, efforts should be made to retire the more expensive debt and thereby reduce the growing interest burden. It has been suggested that a limit on the increase in the public debt as a ratio of total expenditure be placed at 15 percent. To bring down the fiscal deficit to below four percent of gross domestic product, it has been suggested this limit be brought down further to 10 percent over a five-year period.
Business Standard
DEPARTMENT OF TELECOMMUNICATION CUTS TENDER REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has decided to slash its tendered requirement of optical fibre cables from 21,000 km to 8,995 km. The tenders have been dogged by controversy since 1995, when former Communication Minister Sukh Ram started favouring a clutch of companies. The latest twist is that the Dot has not only decided to reduce the requirement in the tender floated in March, by almost two-thirds in violation of its laiddown guidelines, but has also decided to counter offering rates of a bid not technically acceptable.
DEBT MARKETS TAKE CENTRE-STAGE

India's debt market has come alive with more than 106.3 billion rupees being mopped up through bonds and debentures during January-August 1996. During the same period last year, only about eight billion rupees was raised through debt issues, according to reliable industry estimates. This year, the debt market appetite is even greater with 200 billion rupees likely to be mobilised, experts say. Permission to foreign institutional investors to have 100 percent investment in debt issues is likely to boost the market further, they said.
Observer
SKYLINE-NEPC GETS NOD FOR AIRBUS IMPORT

Airbus Industries has entered the private airlines field in India. The Aircraft Acquisition Committee (AAC) has approved in principle Skyline-NEPC's application for the import of European Consortium planes. The private domestic airliners, so far, were dominated by the US based aircraft major Boeing. Besides the Skyline application, AAC is understood to have considered a further 19 requests for aircraft acquisition. The names of the companies were not immediately available.
Business Line
ESSAR OIL PLANS TO SCALE UP EURO ISSUE

Essar Oil Ltd plans to go for an international offering of $250 millions. Essar erlier had planned to raise three billion rupees through an international offering during 1996/97 to part finance its nine million TPA grassroots petroleum refinery project. The company is likely to make the Euro issue during 1997. According to the company, the change in the plans were due to the likely shortfall in raising finances from the public, particularly by way of further calls in view of the existing depressed market conditions.
